But the promotion queue should carry the tension explicitly and future motion promotions should cite it. NOT self-resolvable — Dave's call whether to (a) treat brand-film rules as out-of-scope for micro-interactions, or (b) constrain future promotions.
Names are never fully capitalised — "CONNECTED MONEY" banned; capitalised first letters + lowercase ("Connected Money"). Action-suggesting multi-word names may close up (PayMe, InvestDirect).

Lock-ups are maintained in text for business propositions — always "HSBC Premier", "HSBC Advance"; the HSBC prefix protocol is HSBC + functional descriptor, with judgment to reduce repetition of "HSBC" in running text.
Labels over invented names for standard services — "Live Chat" is a recognised label and needs no name ("Chat To Us" adds complexity). First question is always "is a name required?".
No new icon, logo or brand identity for a name — names follow the current brand identity guidelines.
Simple pages; only elements relevant to the current task. Design-review-level rule; success depends on the rest of the section.
Page-length caps (at 1280×1024): index pages ≤4 vertical view lengths (non-mobile), article pages ≤5.
Separate sections clearly: ≥20px whitespace between sections; separators/control boundaries ≥3:1 contrast (best practice 4.5:1).
Important information top, above the fold; page purpose determinable without scrolling (1280×1024); front-load information. Equal-importance items: alphabetical or chronological.
Every page carries a short purpose summary — in the heading structure, banner, or first paragraph.
Banner/hero caps: initial images/banners ≤30% of page height; carousels and videos ≤30% (at 1280×1024).
Symmetry + layout stability: max 2 different column layouts per page; no significant mid-page layout changes; grid on homepages, single column on content pages.

Links and buttons visibly clickable: underline links; visited links change colour (best practice); button boundaries ≥3:1. ⚠ The :visited leg is a REAL canon gap — no snippet or canon.css styles :visited at all (checked 2026-07-02). 📌 RULED (Dave, 2026-07-02 eve): neuro best practice adopted as direction — visited links should differ in colour; implement at the next Links touch (supercharge candidate territory — don't over-polish pre-uplift), then review the result.

Avoid lots of bright colours: soft, harmonious combinations; bright colours ≤20% of screen content. Autistic users prefer low-contrast schemes — note this is about AREA of saturation, not permission to break contrast floors (floors still apply).

Minimum font size 12pt (exceptions: sub/superscript, T&Cs, related). ⚠ pt-vs-px: 12pt = 16px CSS at the standard 96dpi reading — under which our S6 (14px) and S7 (12px) standard-text sizes would fail; under a loose "12pt≈12px" reading our scale complies (S7=12px floor, 12px reserved for legal = mirrors the exception). The web type scale page and the store both treat 14px/12px as legitimate.

Line height ≥1.5× font size; paragraph spacing ≥2× font size. WCAG 1.4.12 receipt. Our scale: S5 16/24 = 1.5 exactly ✓; S6 14/20 ≈ 1.43 ✗; S7 12/16 ≈ 1.33 ✗ — same family of tension as neuro-016/webf-031; the brand's own scale sits below the neuro floor for small sizes.
≤4 sentences per paragraph; ≤240 characters per sentence (incl. spaces).
Don't interrupt text flow with images; callout quotes only at section ends; no scroll-stoppers.
Bold for phrases only — never whole sections/lists; emphasis not structure.
Clear, concise language at the audience's reading age (WCAG 3.1.5 receipt; does not impact regulatory requirements).

Avoid metaphors and ambiguity. The standard EXPLICITLY flags the tension: tone of voice supports "conversational, informal" style, but literal readers need unambiguous writing. ✅ RECONCILED 2026-07-02 by the tone-of-voice ingest — the brand's own standard partitions the licence: expressive is SURFACE-scoped (headlines, good news, marketing), literalness is FUNCTION-scoped (actions, instructions, warnings) — see `tone-of-voice.md` F2 + tov-019/031/046 (three literalness receipts). Not a contradiction, a partition.
Avoid jargon/abbreviations/acronyms/idioms; define acronyms on the page (WCAG 3.1.3/3.1.4 kin; Style Guide has further guidance).
Icons/visuals support text, never replace it — content must remain comprehensible with all images and icons removed.
Simple images, understood within ~2 seconds; single object in focus. Image content never the sole carrier of information.
Meaningful images only — congruent with the page story, adding value/clarity.
Background images sparingly; no content/form inputs overlaid on decorative images; uniform-texture backgrounds acceptable; non-patterned backgrounds on content pages.
Text intro above every video (what it's about + implied length).

Attention-attracting movement is a LAST resort — use size/colour/font emphasis first. BUT: "small, animated movement of an arrow when moused over communicated that the section was clickable... limited and explainable, users did not find it disturbing" — an empirical receipt that small, purposeful HOVER motion aids comprehension.

Small-type neuro-compliance cluster. neuro-016 (12pt minimum, strict reading = 16px) + neuro-019 (≥1.5 line-height; S6/S7 sit at 1.43/1.33) both indict the brand's OWN type scale for small sizes if read strictly. Since the type scale page and the toolkit export agree on S6/S7, loose readings are almost certainly intended (12pt≈12px; 1.5× aspirational for body = S5 ✓). 📌 RULED (Dave, 2026-07-02 eve): record-to-review only — "this is one that will definitely change anyway" (the refresh will re-cut the type scale); do NOT chase Create Direct on it.

Calm-by-default vs expressive register. neuro-006 (hero ≤30% height), neuro-014 (bright colours ≤20% of screen), neuro-001/-028 (simplicity) collectively define a measurable "calm ceiling". The expressive register (charter §4, dual-live palettes) pushes the other way. These are not contradictions — they're the two dials of the fixed/flex charter with NUMBERS on the sober side for the first time. Generation consequence: the register spread should treat neuro caps as the sober register's defaults and as advisory signals elsewhere.

Communication guidance is a hub we did not descend — 7 scenario subpages (meetings, multimedia, media, digital content, internal comms, surveys, social media). Scenario 4 (digital content) is the engine-relevant one.

Style: cinematic, immersive, human, authentic — frame stories; human perspective required, people optional; muted, sophisticated tones (never too vibrant); red appears tactically and NATURALLY (warmth in lens/scene, not forced accents); lead with photography as the principal creative medium.

HARD bans: no Generative AI, mixed media or CGI-rendered elements in imagery; no montages/composites; no staged/posed/clichéd shots; no text as a mask. ⚠ The gen-AI ban is PIPELINE-CRITICAL: a generation engine must never fabricate photographic imagery — photography comes from the Global Image Library/approved sources only. Direct kin of the gen-AI governance regime (gai-*); Apollo's imagery story = retrieval from licensed libraries, full stop.

Shot vocabulary: cinematic · people (real moments; diversity; disability shown positively; natural warmth in skin tones) · landscapes/cityscapes (lived-in viewpoints, not landmark clichés) · objects (lower-funnel, curated, product-linked) · textural (macro) · abstract (mood, photography-based).
Every pictogram carries a label or copy that underpins its meaning — no exceptions (unlike icons' universal-meaning carve-out).
Not a replacement for icons or illustrations; never interchange.
Don't use pictograms as a replacement for a hero illustration.
Use levels to reflect message importance; don't mix levels in components representing messages of equal prominence.

Keep metaphors simple and globally recognisable; avoid unnecessary abstraction (bowl + steam, not the bowl's contents). Abstract designs only for figurative concepts (FX, sustainability) and never reliant on prior knowledge.
No designs without a clear relationship to the message they support.
Don't place pictograms on a red background — interferes with the red accent and causes contrast issues with the primary form.

≥3:1 contrast against the background in all placements, with clearly descriptive alt text. L1 on dark backgrounds only with white lines; L1 over photography only where the background doesn't compromise contrast; nothing on visually busy imagery.
No drop shadows — elevation is functional-only (an object moving over another), which a pictogram never needs.
Digital: minimum 60px, maximum 192px, proportional scaling at 2px intervals. Below 60px, use an icon instead.
Never squash, stretch, skew or distort; scale with locked aspect ratio.
Don't position different-scale pictograms immediately next to one another in common components; max 3 distinct sizes per experience, logically chosen.
Non-digital (print, physical): scale proportionally to the format with sufficient clear space; legibility at small sizes.

Pictograms are a component-library gap. The engine's 38 components include icons (sprite + gate) but no pictogram asset class at all — no tokens, no assets, no manifest entry. If generated experiences ever include pictogram-bearing patterns (empty states, onboarding, confirmation illustrations), this class needs onboarding: distinct contrast rule (3:1 + alt), distinct size floor (60px), level system, and a sourcing pipeline (create.hsbc asset library + "Pictogram creation" approvals process for new symbols). Parked — no current snippet uses pictograms.

The HSBC voice = four principles: Human, Insightful, Confident, Intelligent wit. Together they are the brand's verbal identity — "customers should be able to recognise us by how we write and speak" the same way they spot the palette and logo.

The voice does not change by channel; the mechanics do. "Our voice doesn't change, regardless of whether we're writing a letter, email, text or tweet" — channel rules (below) tune length and structure, never identity.

Say 'we' and 'you'. First person plural for the bank, second person for the reader. "We're writing to you about your current account", never "Today HSBC is communicating to all current account customers".

Use contractions — single contractions only. I'm, we'll, you're, can't, won't, don't. Never double contractions ('wouldn't've', 'shouldn't've'). Writing words out in full is allowed for deliberate emphasis ("I will").

Formal→human word substitutions (merged principles-page + FAQ tables, 17 pairs): advise/inform→tell · assist→help · cease→stop · commence→start · continue→carry on · converse→talk · endeavour→try · enquire/request→ask · ensure→make sure · funds→money · obtain/receive→get · provide→give · require→need · therefore→so.
Plain English, no financial or legal jargon; familiar words wherever possible. Readability is framed as an inclusion measure (age, education, ESL, text-reader users, ADD/autism/dyslexia/dyspraxia).
Readability floor: Flesch-Kincaid 70+ / grade ≤7 (reading age 11) as the general bar for all writing. Source calibration: Harry Potter ≈ the bar; Time magazine ≈ grade 12.
Readability targets by artefact type (Flesch Reading Ease): internal email 60–70+ · customer email 60–70+ · customer letter 60+ · social 70+ · report 50+ · technical report 45+ · T&Cs 40+.
Active voice, not passive. "We'll send you a closing statement", not "a closing statement will be sent". Passive hides the actor and cools the tone.
Main point first. Only what the reader needs to know. What you think the key point is and what the reader needs aren't always the same — decide what matters to *them* before writing.

Summary subheadings that carry the key message — skimmable by design; explicitly motivated by a11y (screen-reader navigation, dyslexia/autism) as well as time-poor readers. Headings should summarise ("Tougher markets, tighter margins"), not label ("Outlook").
If something is changing, always say why — especially unwelcome news; reasons in ≤2 sentences, no regulation or internal-process detail.

No hedging: banned commitment-hedge phrases — 'we're committed to', 'we endeavour to', 'we aim to', 'The Board is committed to'. Say what we're doing: "We're asking you for this information to protect you…". Hedges "make us appear unreliable and non-committal".
Always say what happens next — even when it's 'nothing'. Every message that shares information ends with what to expect; "even if no more action is needed, be sure to say that clearly."

Wit is a flourish, not a register. Source, explicitly: "it's more of a flourish than something we use throughout – it works best in headlines or when we're giving good news." Gradient as stated: advertising/marketing = dial up · good news + headlines = home turf · functional messages = "quite subtle" · important/clear-and- straightforward messages = don't distract · difficult situations (bereavement, pandemic) = zero. This is the fixed/flex temperature dial with a source receipt — see Findings F1.
Specific beats generic: use references that resonate with the named audience (UHNW legacy framing vs student 'pop into a branch'). No two audiences the same.
No clichés or stock expressions ("24 hours a day, 7 days a week" = "a cliché any bank could use"). Fresh perspective instead.

Colloquialisms show local expertise — BUT functional messages stay literal. Source, verbatim: "neurodiverse readers may interpret language very literally. So stick to clear, unambiguous phrases in functional messages, or when telling readers to take an action." Reconciles neuro-024 — see Findings F2.
Don't define the audience too narrowly — readers have overlapping identities (race, nationality, orientation, gender identity, parenthood, neurodiversity, disability, ESL).

Gender-neutral defaults: no gendered titles when unknown (use 'Hello [Name]'); -person job titles (chairperson, businessperson, police officer); gender-neutral social roles ('parents/caregivers', not 'mothers'); they/them until told otherwise.

Coded-language ban list: blacklist/whitelist → blocklist/allowlist · master-/slave- → primary/secondary · 'long time no see' → 'it's been a while' · 'ethnic' as qualifier → name the actual group/market · 'illegal immigrants' → 'undocumented person'.
No umbrella terms (BAME, BME, catch-all 'Asian'); name communities properly; capitalise Black as ethnic/cultural adjective (AP style).

Vary example names and cultural references in placeholders, pre-populated fields, and scenario copy across cultures, backgrounds, faiths. ENGINE-CRITICAL: this is a rule about *generated fixture data* — our snippet/gallery placeholder names are in scope.

People-first language: person with a disability · has epilepsy, never 'is an epileptic' · never 'suffers from' · 'a reader over 65', never 'elderly'. Identity- first accepted where communities choose it (autistic, Deaf); person-first when unsure.

Unwelcome news: MORE human, not more formal. Formality under stress is named as a misconception that "harms the customer experience". Readability stays at grade ≤7; don't dress bad news as good news or force a positive.

Sorry once, early, plainly — and only for things we control. "We're sorry for the mistake." Banned insincere apologies: 'we apologise for any inconvenience caused' · 'please accept our sincerest apologies' · 'regretfully, mistakes were made'. No apology for regulatory/market changes.

No throat-clearing openers: 'It has come to our attention…' · 'Following a recent review…' · 'As you'll be aware…'. Main point early; for very bad news a one-line preparatory frame is allowed ("We're writing to let you know that…") — and the main message may sit in the heading/subject itself.

Unwelcome news ends with options + a warm route in: when the change hits, what impact, what to do with questions, alternatives (switchable accounts, nearby branches), prominent placement, never an abrupt ending.

Sensitive subjects: no euphemisms. 'Has died', not 'passed away'; the person's name, not 'the deceased'/'your late husband'. Plain and warm, not sentimental ("insincere coming from a bank"); euphemisms are also a literalness barrier (neuro-024 receipt).
Internal comms: same standards + Smart Brevity numbers — updates <300 words, paragraphs 1–2 sentences, open with "What's new" / "Why it matters", sentences <25 words, subheading every 3–4 paragraphs.
Good news: no self-congratulation. Banned: 'you'll be delighted to know' + subjective adjectives 'amazing', 'fantastic', 'brilliant' ("salesy and presumptuous"). Let the benefit speak.

Calls to action: one message per communication; open AND close with the CTA; signpost with action headings ('What to do now'); consequences stated as fact, not threat; specific deep links, not homepages; numbers + hours in body text, never small print; avoid asterisks/small print generally.
Hard-sell ban list: 'simply' (as in 'simply visit') · 'Did you know…?' · 'remember'/'don't forget' · 'Hurry!' · 'Free!' · 'Dear Valued Customer'.

Process guidance: soften imperatives ('You'll need to…'), warm form-field labels ('Your details', not 'Account holder's details'; 'Please tell us', not 'Please indicate'), steps in the customer's question-order, say where they are in the process. ENGINE-CRITICAL: form-label warmth + progress-location are component rules (Input-fields, Progress trackers).

Forms & attachments: first person; active; ≤2 enclosures; label variable parts (page/section refs); summary paragraph atop long documents; pre-populate what we know; boxes not lines; return-checklist; benefit-framed instructions.
Device-agnostic language: 'select', never 'click'; never describe UI visually. Writing must work on desktop, mobile, tablet. Canon swept 2026-07-02: 0 signals.
Email: subject carries the why in <8 words; spam-trigger words avoided ('Free', 'Email', 'Buy', 'Cash', '100%', 'Income'); two-scroll length cap; CTA at open and close.

Web/PDF: sentences <15 words; ≤3 sentences per paragraph; F-pattern layout awareness (key content top-left, never bottom-right); more subheadings than print; subheadings summarise the paragraph below. ENGINE-CRITICAL: these are the copy numbers for every generated screen.

Greetings/sign-offs matrix by line of business: Retail letter 'Dear [first name]'/'Yours sincerely' · Retail email 'Hello'/'Thanks' · Retail text 'Hi [first name]'/'Thanks or thank you' · PB + CMB/GBM letter 'Dear [preferred name]'/'Yours sincerely' · PB + CMB/GBM email 'Hello'/'Thank you' · PB + CMB/GBM text 'Dear [preferred name]'/'Thank you'. Team sign-offs ('Your HSBC Advance Team') unless a named person can respond directly. Name unknown → drop the salutation entirely.

The voice sits mid-scale on formality — never slang, never old-fashioned — so it can adapt per market. Named calibrations: Australia = most informal · France/ Argentina = more traditional (vous/vos) · India/Malaysia = "a few degrees towards formal" (social hierarchy). Clarity always outranks the local adjustment.
No idioms where non-native speakers may miss them: 'get started', not 'get the ball rolling'. Local spelling/terminology honoured (cheque/check; Secure Key/ Security Device HK).
Never red typography for headlines or body copy — red only for text links (CTAs) and "specific digital toolkit use-cases".

Readability numbers: body line length 60–80 Latin characters (avg); headline length 20–50 characters (avg); no orphans (single word alone on the last line of a heading/ paragraph); no widows (word/short group starting a new column or page).
No italics — not licensed, and harder to read, especially for people with dyslexia.

Emphasis = Univers Bold only, keywords/phrases not sections. No underline for emphasis (underline = links only — neuro-007 dual-source) · no shapes/graphic devices · no drop shadows on text · no outlines or graphic styling on type.
Type colour: dark-on-light, light-on-dark; no highlighted type blocks; no long-form copy on red or coloured backgrounds; consider size/scale for headline type on coloured backgrounds.
Headlines get breathing space — keep body copy apart from creative headline typography.
Hierarchy: lead with a short, instantly understandable headline + concise body; sub-headings distinct from both; CTA sits away from body with more weight, without competing with the headline.

Three cost-0 gate candidates surfaced: no-italics scan (type25-007), no-text-shadow scan (type25-008), red-text-role check (type25-003) — all passed canon with zero occurrences. RULED by Dave 2026-07-03: STRAIGHT TO BLOCKING (his override of the advisory-first convention — zero occurrences + exact checks = the advisory step buys nothing). ENACTED as snippet-gate check 6 (`_validate_snippets.py`), bite-tested ×3 in `_tests/test_gates.py`; red text stays legal via the rag/error role token (var(--error)) and CTA roles — the gate bans the raw-hex role bypass.
Only use brand-approved fonts, weights and colours.
All text legible and ≥4.5:1 contrast.
Never use red typography except within specific digital toolkit use-cases. Sharpens the col26 red-text rule: the exception scope is toolkit-defined (e.g. CTA links), not designer judgment.

"We don't use uppercase or italics lettering — use sentence case." ⚑ This makes the house sentence-case rule (and the G5 all-caps advisory check) source-backed at brand level — and extends it: *italics are also out*. Informs the open all-caps scope ruling on Dave's desk: the source is brand-wide, favouring canon-wide over brief-scoped.
Only use lighter font weights for creative headline treatments; favour lighter weights generally, bolder weights only for occasional emphasis (a word, a subheading).
Expressive headlines — emphasis, pace, personality without losing clarity; fewer words; never obscure or break a word into illegibility.
Balanced bilingual — Latin/Chinese/Arabic given comparable prominence, unified not "translated"; balance layout, hierarchy, spacing, line length.
Clear type hierarchy — scale/weight/spacing/placement signal reading order; limit weight levels to the minimum; max two main fonts with a bold option.

Headlines: lightest weights (Ultra Light, Thin, Light) at larger sizes; heavier only for a clear hierarchy shift or single emphasis point. Never bold an entire headline — one or two words at most. Body: light/regular. "If everything's bold, nothing is."
Hierarchy depth: 3–4 levels (L1 headline, L2, supporting, body).

Latin: 12pt minimum, print AND digital. Captions/small legal copy may go to 6pt minimum. Ultra Light/Thin forbidden at small sizes (line too thin to be legible). Chinese (MYing Hei): 14pt body minimum. Arabic: 12pt (as Latin).

Black/dark-grey on light · white/light-grey on dark · NO other colours for typography, ever. White-only on HSBC Red and supporting reds; no long-form copy on red or coloured backgrounds; no highlighted type blocks; over photography black or white only.
Headline-on-photography contrast: 3:1 large AA · 4.5:1 small AA · 7:1 AAA.

"Don't overlay text on gradient backgrounds" (+ digital: verify at viewpoints, no unreadable wrap). ⚠ Collides with charter §4's expressive gradient unlock for surfaces/heroes — heroes normally carry headlines. 📌 PARKED 2026-07-02 (Dave) → ruled at the component-finessing pass, alongside mot-007 ("too expressive" family). Interim discipline: no gradient-hero generation; gradient surfaces are treated as text-free zones until ruled (conservative reading holds by default). Candidate mechanisations noted for the pass: text-free-zone gate (no text node over gradient surface) vs worst-point contrast sampling (≥4.5:1 at the ramp's weakest point, render-based).

Latin headlines: −15 to −30 tracking; leading = size +3pt (50pt → 53pt). Latin body: −5 to −10 tracking; leading "1.1×" — ⚠ but the page's own example is 12pt → 16pt (1.33×), and Chinese body says 1.1× with example 14pt → 18pt (1.29×). Stated ratio and worked examples disagree — likely "1.1×" should read differently or the examples embed channel-specific values.
Chinese headlines: leading 1.25×; body 0 to +10 tracking. Fine-tune Chinese punctuation spacing; refine baselines when mixing scripts.
No wide kerning that breaks legibility; not too tight either.

Title case AND sentence case are the brand-legal casings; uppercase banned outside acronyms (explicitly: harder to read, reduces word shapes, dyslexia/low-vision cost). Note: the house rule (sentence case ONLY, no title case) is *stricter* than brand — house wins locally, no conflict. ✅ ENACTED 2026-07-02 (Dave ruling): canon-wide sweep done — 14 snippets + gallery chrome de-capped (caps tracking removed with it, Eyebrow precedent), canon.css regenerated, 0 signals; check PROMOTED advisory → blocking (`_validate_snippets.py` check 4, acronym-run exemption, bite-tested ×2 in `_tests/test_gates.py`).

Left-aligned is primary; centred sparingly (short headings/labels/callouts, small word counts); right rare ("Headline A of the magnetic type construct"); body copy stays horizontal. Never justified (rivers); avoid hyphenation — rebalance lines instead.
Size ratio 1.0× Latin : 0.85× Chinese (perceived-height parity); Chinese one weight step thicker than Latin (Univers Ultra Light ↔ MYingHei Thin · Thin ↔ Light · Light ↔ Regular · Regular ↔ Medium).
Balanced dual language — Latin + Chinese + Arabic get comparable prominence, "unified, rather than 'translated' or secondary"; balance layout/hierarchy/spacing/ line length.

Give imagery room to breathe: type frames the focal point, sits in clean negative space or along natural composition lines; grids + rule of thirds; clear visual path — headline first, then the image's key detail. Centre alignment is now legitimate in named cases: ambient photography without a focal point (Iconic Hexagon central, with or without text), magnetic headlines centred. ⚠ DELTA vs 2025's "never centre-align creative headlines with hexagons" (type25-017).

Over-photography watch-outs: legibility first — avoid busy areas, high-contrast edges, faces; safe placement, sufficient contrast, "(where needed) a subtle gradient/ overlay, rather than heavy effects"; respect the subject — never cover focal points/ faces/brand cues. ⚠ DELTA vs 2025's flat "no treatments — adjust the asset" (type25-013): the refresh PERMITS subtle overlays as a contrast aid. Interim reading: overlay-as- contrast-aid OK (it's also the dark-mode imagery mechanism, webf-008), decorative effects still banned.

Magnetic headline (NEW construct): an Iconic Hexagon sits at the CENTRE of the headline line as visual anchor/pivot; words "magnetised" around it; vertical alignment to the hexagon's 5 vertices, baselines to hexagon geometry; photography stays the hero (magnetic block moves to give the subject space; stacked/side variants; centred over ambient scenes); rule of thirds guides, not strict. This is the brand-campaign headline construct — the 2026 replacement register for 2025's big-and-light/small-and-bold pairing. ⚠ DELTA: 2025's "only Big-and-Light and Small-and-Bold" takeaway has no 2026 equivalent; the refresh's named types are "over photography" and "magnetic".

Inclusion test before any asset: what's the intent? does it help understanding? does it distract, obscure or slow the user? No contextually-irrelevant images "for the sake of layout or design" — "sometimes less is more".

Attribute taxonomy — every asset is functional (icons, avatars, logos), informational (product photos, infographics, diagrams, charts) or complementary (photography, illustration) — defined by content nature, not media type. The placement rules below key off this.

Visual-engagement tiers set the imagery budget per page type: HIGH (home, hub, landing, promotion) = complementary allowed throughout · MEDIUM (product, service, article) = complementary minimal — header or start-of-section only; informational/ functional carry the weight · LOW (applications, processes) = ONLY assets fundamental to the task; complementary at most at the very start or completion. ENGINE-CRITICAL: a page-type parameter that caps complementary imagery — the sober register's imagery numbers by another route.
Onboarding: new-to-HSBC users may get more complementary assets (if they enhance, never distract); existing customers get focused informational/functional for new features.

Pattern consistency across the journey: same asset type for the same pattern everywhere (an illustration on one confirmation page = illustrations on ALL confirmation-class pages); logged-on and logged-off experiences consistent. Named surfaces where this is critical: applications · onboarding · coach marks · tutorials · alerts messaging · status codes (eg 404) · empty states. ENGINE-CRITICAL → confirmation/success gap-pattern + any empty-state pattern get an asset-type contract.
Hierarchy: assets supporting the primary goal outrank secondary-goal assets; avoid conflicts of attention (order, scale, space, contrast, balance).

Re-use rules: an asset re-appears only in the same context/metaphor/purpose. Never the same thumbnail linking to different content; never the same hero for different articles/products; never an icon outside its functional context (source example: a memo icon representing fraud content). ENGINE-CRITICAL: the icon SEMANTIC-fit layer on top of the icon-source gate — provenance says which icons exist, this says an icon must mean what it shows.

Responsive behaviour: test assets across devices; photography adapts by ratio crops; illustrations may need reformatting AND line-weight adjustment per layout/ size. Brand-source receipt for the dynamic-weight concept — the brand itself says line weight is context-dependent.
Light/dark modes: assets may need per-mode exports; icons black-in-light get value-reversed in dark (can be code-level). Receipt for the icon-contrast-delta work and mode-aware asset handling.
Quality bar: sharp, high-quality, tested on low- and high-DPI — or NO asset at all ("better not to use any visual assets" than bad ones).

Placement taxonomy: hero · display · spot · thumbnail · interface, with attribute legality per placement (hero = complementary/informational · interface = NEVER complementary · thumbnail = any) + the placements-by-type matrix (verbatim in `_sources`: video/animation top out at spot; photography/illustration reach thumbnail; avatars/icons/logos live spot→interface; favicons interface-only).

Aspect ratios: video/animation 16:9 standard (21:9, 4:3, 1:1 alternates); photography/illustration/infographics 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1 (reversible for portrait); icons/avatars 1:1 square — "icons and avatars that appear rounded are likely to have masked the square asset using code"; third-party logos 16:9/4:3. The rounding-is-a-code-mask line is the official mechanics behind the Badge+Avatar round exemption: the ASSET stays square, the mask rounds.

The page's numeric rules (absent from the 2026 distillation): clear space = 1× hexagon height on all sides; minimum size = 7mm hexagon height / 105×20px / 26×7mm; positioning = top-left or bottom-left, inset 1× hexagon from edges (exceptions: video open/end frames, eye-line adjustment out-of-home).

Masthead contract: the Masterbrand logo appears in ALL digital mastheads; clicking it always returns to the root of the CURRENT business line — never cross-line, orientation over surprise. ENGINE-CRITICAL → the Header/masthead component (deferred but queued) inherits this behaviour contract.

Never-rules: no new lock-ups from text for departments/programmes/products; never distort, recolour, reorient or recreate; hexagon-only use needs Create Direct approval AND 'HSBC' context nearby (app tile, profile avatar, favicon); never the legacy Times New Roman logo; third-party use follows the TMLA process; Brand Promise lock-up never wraps lines.

Variant selection on photographic backgrounds: primary (red hexagon/white infill/black type) on light; white-wordmark version on dark-where-red-reads; mono black on light print, mono-reversed white on dark or HSBC-red; white infill never on mono versions. Expands logo26's dark = full-colour-negative rule with the legibility ladder.

No Generative AI, mixed media or CGI-rendered elements in imagery — ALSO the 2025 rule. photo26-002 is therefore vintage-STABLE, not a refresh novelty: the ban has held across both standards. Second receipt for the pipeline-critical rule (engine generates experiences, never photographic assets; library retrieval only).

D&I imagery rules: diverse representation across markets; no stereotypes or clichés; represent LGBTQ+ people; portray people with disabilities living their lives — never make the perceived difference the focus; localisation sensitivity per market. Imagery-side kin of tov-025's fixture diversity.
Creative considerations (explicitly optional): natural hints of red; hexagon- geometry angles, never a forced 45°; wide 'opening up' frames + intimate close crops.
Photography textures always use the red/white/grey palette.
Limit colour, especially HSBC red, in dark mode — replace some light-mode colour with white/grey; red kept strategic (primary CTA, hexagon). Every use of red evaluated.

Light-bleed compensation. Strong light-on-dark makes type/icon strokes look heavier; counteract with light grey, lowered white opacity, or lighter background — but contrast must still pass accessibility.
Dark mode needs more negative space — dark backgrounds make the same layout feel more closed-in.

Level taxonomy: 0 = base content (body, imagery, cards, buttons — NEVER elevated) · 1 = sticky content (top navigation, drawer, tooltip) · 2 = modality (partial modals, dialogs) · 3 = notifications (snackbars). Elements contained within a level do not display further elevation.
Shadow = specified depth (higher level → deeper shadow); overlay = large, unspecified depth, used to focus. Never display both on the same element/pattern.
No purely aesthetic shadows (inner or outer) — elevation is functional.
No elevation on patterns that move within level-0 content (e.g. an accordion pushing content down).
